Definition: flesh (from its freshness); by extension, body, person; also (by euphemistically) the pudenda of a man
BiblicalUsage: Basar is flesh, the body, the stuff we are made of. Adam calls Eve bone of his bones and flesh of his flesh, God says His Spirit will not always strive with man because he is flesh, Isaiah says all flesh will see the glory of the Lord together, and Ezekiel promises God will take away the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe flesh is the Bible's word for our frailty and our hope at once, because the same flesh that fails is the flesh God promises to renew. He made us flesh, He came in flesh, and I hold that the God who gives a heart of flesh is the God who will raise our flesh in glory.
